purpose: Pinned upstream source evidence for the session lifecycle-status CONTENT that the picker's status column renders. The retained spec §F names the tag/colour functions only; `upstream-status-attr/` pinned how a status maps to a tag word and to ink. This packet pins the missing half: how the reference *derives* the status (`classify_session_status` + `SessionDB.session_lifecycle_statuses`) from the last message row of each session, so the claim "Rust can only ever show `done`/`empty`" can be judged against the pinned contract instead of prose.
fetched_with: gh api repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/git/blobs/166c39a519750cefa7116f92ecbd73c35bfd2ad9 | base64 -d (no direct network from the sandbox). Re-verified in-repo with `git hash-object hermes_state.py` == blob_sha_git, which is the same check `reference.json` used for the tree.

relevant_lines.classify_session_status: 5120-5145 (error finish_reason first, then assistant+tool_calls -> interrupted, user/tool -> interrupted, otherwise complete)
relevant_lines.session_lifecycle_statuses: 12400-12445 (one MAX(id)-per-session join, never a transcript scan; sessions with no message row default to 'empty')

excerpt_file: hermes_state_excerpt.py (verbatim line ranges, headers added; the full file is retained next to it and is the authoritative copy)

contract_as_read.empty: no messages row at all for that session id
contract_as_read.error: last message row's finish_reason, stripped and lowercased, is one of error/agent_error/content_filter (checked BEFORE role)
contract_as_read.interrupted: last row is role assistant with a non-NULL tool_calls column, or role user, or role tool
contract_as_read.complete: any other last row (including unrecognized roles); the reference documents this as a benign default
contract_as_read.tag_rendering: the tag word comes from `_session_status_tag` (complete->done, interrupted->intr, error->err, empty->empty, unknown->'-'); ink mapping and the tag column are pinned in ../upstream-status-attr/provenance.json
contract_as_read.failure_mode: `_annotate_session_statuses` swallows any error from the status query and leaves rows untagged, so the picker renders '-' rather than failing

corroboration: retained capture picker-normal-100x30: the Python side draws `intr` on a non-cursor row with palette index 3, i.e. the interrupted branch of this contract is observable in the pinned reference recording
docs/hermes-ui-spec/017/evidence/upstream-status-attr/provenance.json: the tag words and ink mapping this content feeds

Rust side today: crates/hermes-cli/src/session_picker.rs collect_rows() sets status to `empty` when a session has no turns and `done` otherwise — the `intr`/`err` branches are unreachable, and docs/PARITY.md records that as the T09 adaptation
limitations: This is upstream source evidence at the pinned commit, not an audit of the user's historical VM installation.

The reference reads `messages.tool_calls` and `messages.finish_reason`, columns the Python schema has and the Rust-created schema (crates/hermes-core/src/session/store.rs) does not; any port decision must say explicitly how each of the two database shapes behaves.
No new pixel capture or acceptance is implied by this packet; it only pins the contract.
